title: Sound Insulation: Key Concepts and Technologies

findings.antecedent: Sound Pressure Level (SPL) before material (SPL1) and after material (SPL2)
findings.quote: NR is calculated by subtracting the SPL after the sound passes through the material (SPL2) from the level before encountering the material (SPL₁)

findings.antecedent: Sound Pressure Level (SPL) without material (SPL1) and with material (SPL2)
findings.quote: IL is calculated using Eq. 2, where SPL1 is the SPL without the material and SPL2 with the material in place.

findings.antecedent: Ratio of transmitted sound intensity (Itransmitted) to incident sound intensity (Iincident)
findings.quote: STL denotes the difference between the incident and transmitted sound intensity levels when sound waves encounter a material.

findings.antecedent: Ratio of absorbed sound energy (Iabsorbed) to incident sound energy (Iincident)
findings.quote: SAC quantifies the ratio of incident sound energy that a material absorbs instead of reflecting it into the environment.

findings.antecedent: One-third octave average of SACs at 250 Hz, 500 Hz, 1000 Hz, and 2000 Hz
findings.quote: NRC is calculated as the one-third octave average of the SACs at four specific frequencies: 250 Hz, 500 Hz, 1000 Hz, and 2000 Hz.

findings.antecedent: Material rigidity (in stiffness region)
findings.consequent: Sound Transmission Loss (STL) at lower frequencies
findings.quote: Edge-constrained stiff barriers effectively block low-frequency sounds with long wavelengths, leading to a higher STL at lower frequencies.

findings.antecedent: Frequency doubling (in stiffness region)
findings.quote: This part of the curve shows a 6 dB decrease in STL for every frequency doubling

findings.antecedent: Material/structure natural vibrations aligning with sound waves (in resonance region)
findings.quote: These variations correspond to the frequencies at which the material or structure's natural vibrations align with the sound waves, potentially enhancing sound transmission

findings.antecedent: Damping (in resonance region)
findings.quote: with low damping, fluctuations lessen; and with high damping, the curve smooths, indicating more effective sound reduction.

findings.antecedent: Barrier mass and frequency (in mass law region)
findings.quote: heavier barriers are more effective at blocking sound, a property that becomes increasingly pronounced at higher frequencies.

findings.antecedent: Frequency doubling (in mass law region)
findings.quote: shows a steady increase of about 6 dB for each frequency doubling

findings.antecedent: Sound wave wavelength matching flexural wavelength in barrier (in coincidence region)
findings.quote: a noticeable dip in the STL curve occurs at a frequency where the sound wave's wavelength is the same size as the flexural wavelength in the barrier, causing increased sound penetration.

findings.antecedent: Material density and mass
findings.quote: Heavier and denser materials generally have higher STL.

findings.antecedent: Material thickness (especially for lower frequencies)
findings.quote: The thickness of a material having a specified density is directly proportional to its STL, especially for lower frequencies.

findings.antecedent: Material stiffness and elastic properties
findings.consequent: Sound transmission efficiency in coincidence region (lower STL)
findings.quote: Stiffer materials can transmit sound more efficiently in the coincidence region, leading to lower STL.

findings.antecedent: Material internal damping
findings.quote: Materials with higher internal damping can convert more sound energy into heat, thus reducing sound transmission.

findings.antecedent: Material resonant frequency
findings.quote: Every material has a resonant frequency at which it vibrates most efficiently. The material can amplify sound at this frequency, reducing its STL.

findings.antecedent: Environmental factors (temperature and humidity)
findings.quote: These environmental factors can change the physical properties of materials, affecting their STL.

findings.antecedent: Sound frequency
findings.quote: Materials exhibit varying STL characteristics across different frequencies.

findings.antecedent: Improper installation (gaps, holes, poor seals)
findings.quote: Improper installation, characterized by gaps, holes, or poor seals, can significantly undermine the STL of a barrier.

findings.antecedent: Using composite materials (layers of different materials)
findings.quote: Using composite materials (e.g., layers of different materials) can enhance STL, as each layer can be engineered to target specific frequencies or sound types for enhanced sound insulation.

findings.antecedent: Flanking paths (indirect routes for sound transmission)
findings.quote: Sound can bypass a soundproof material through “Flanking paths,” which refers to indirect routes for sound transmissions, such as through ceilings, floors, and adjoining walls.

findings.antecedent: Metamaterial-based thin plates with subwavelength resonator arrays
findings.quote: Metamaterial-based thin plates equipped with subwavelength resonator arrays exhibit higher STL than conventional bare plates

findings.antecedent: Thick metamaterial plate with spring-mass resonators
findings.quote: A thick metamaterial plate with spring-mass resonators can achieve STL up to 72 dB at 2 kHz, significantly surpassing the performance of homogeneous plates

findings.antecedent: Membrane-type acoustic metamaterials
findings.quote: Membrane-type acoustic metamaterials provide excellent sound attenuation in the low-frequency range, with STL being strongly influenced by the attached mass and membrane properties

findings.antecedent: Damping within metamaterials (in resonators and host structures)
findings.quote: The critical role of damping within metamaterials for vibroacoustic attenuation performance, particularly the impact of damping in resonators and host structures on STL, is highlighted

findings.antecedent: Lightweight multilayer honeycomb membrane-type acoustic metamaterials
findings.quote: Lightweight multilayer honeycomb membrane-type acoustic metamaterials (Fig. 5a) defy the traditional mass law to achieve exceptional STL while maintaining a low weight

findings.antecedent: Acoustic metamaterials incorporating piezoelectric patches
findings.quote: Acoustic metamaterials incorporating piezoelectric patches offer dual functionality in sound insulation and energy harvesting, achieving over 20 dB STL and a maximum energy conversion efficiency of up to 15.3%

findings.antecedent: Helmholtz cavity-based acoustic metamaterials
findings.quote: Helmholtz cavity-based acoustic metamaterials demonstrate exceptional sound insulation performance, particularly in isolating low-frequency noise

findings.antecedent: Metamaterial barriers based on cellular structures
findings.consequent: STL in low-frequency range without excessive mass
findings.quote: Metamaterial barriers based on cellular structures (Fig. 5b) provide high STL in the low-frequency range without the addition of excessive mass

findings.antecedent: Damping design of resonators in locally resonant metamaterial plates
findings.quote: the damping design of the resonators affecting the acoustic insulation performance

findings.antecedent: Coupled-resonance acoustic metamaterials
findings.quote: Coupled-resonance acoustic metamaterials promise broadband and intense STL

findings.antecedent: Metamaterials designed with meta-porous materials tuned at exceptional points
findings.consequent: Sound attenuation in acoustic ducts at low frequencies
findings.quote: Metamaterials designed with meta-porous materials (Fig. 5d) tuned at exceptional points optimize sound attenuation in acoustic ducts at low frequencies

findings.antecedent: Perforations in thick perforated panels
findings.consequent: Coincidence effect at critical frequencies (enhancing STL above 630 Hz)
findings.quote: perforations reduce the coincidence effect at critical frequencies, enhancing STL above 630 Hz

findings.antecedent: Smaller hole diameters in micro-perforated panels
findings.consequent: STL due to resistive parts in hole impedance
findings.quote: smaller diameters in micro-perforated panels resulting in higher STL due to resistive parts in the hole impedance

findings.antecedent: 3D-printed bio-degradable micro-perforated panels with varying perforation cross-sections
findings.consequent: Sound absorption compared to uniform cross-sectional perforation
findings.quote: acoustic behavior of 3D-printed bio-degradable micro-perforated panels (Fig. 6) with varying perforation cross-sections indicates better sound absorption than uniform cross-sectional perforation

findings.antecedent: Perforation diameter in perforated-natural fiber sandwich panels
findings.quote: The STL of perforated-natural fiber sandwich panels is notably influenced by perforation diameter, with a hybrid panel combining pineapple leaf fiber and a 3 mm perforation achieving the highest STL among tested samples

findings.antecedent: Small perforations in corrugated sandwich panels
findings.consequent: Low-frequency sound absorption and transmission loss
findings.quote: Small perforations in corrugated sandwich panels significantly enhance low-frequency sound absorption and transmission loss

findings.antecedent: Panel's perforation rate and elastic properties in underwater flexible micro-perforated panels
findings.quote: Underwater flexible micro-perforated panels (Fig. 7) show that the panel's perforation rate and elastic properties significantly influence STL

findings.antecedent: Micro-perforated panels coupled with honeycomb panels (considering air cavities)
findings.quote: Micro-perforated panels coupled with honeycomb panels consider air cavities for offshore plants, showing a significant increase in STL at mid-frequencies

findings.antecedent: Perforating honeycomb walls of a honeycomb sandwich panel
findings.quote: the effect of perforating honeycomb walls of a honeycomb sandwich panel on dynamic bending stiffness and STL highlights the significance of the perforation design

findings.antecedent: Glass bead volume fraction and sound frequency in inorganic particulate-filled polymer composites
findings.quote: STL increases with the glass bead volume fraction and sound frequency.

findings.antecedent: Size of glass beads (given constant volume fraction) in inorganic particulate-filled polymer composites
findings.quote: it decreases when the size of the glass beads is increased, given a constant volume fraction

findings.antecedent: Addition of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) into Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS) composites
findings.quote: The addition of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) into Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS) composites has been shown to significantly enhance STL

findings.antecedent: Particle type and composite structure in polymer/inorganic particle composites (PP/nano-CaCO3, ABS/CaCO3, PVC/hollow glass bead)
findings.quote: Further investigations into polymer/inorganic particle composites, such as PP/nano-CaCO3, ABS/CaCO3, and PVC/hollow glass bead (HGB), have confirmed the significant role of particle type and composite structure on STL

findings.antecedent: Adding CNTs and foaming to wood fiber-low-density polyethylene (LDPE) composites
findings.consequent: STL (especially at medium and higher frequencies)
findings.quote: adding CNTs and foaming to wood fiber-low-density polyethylene (LDPE) composites has improved STL, especially at medium and higher frequencies

findings.antecedent: Hybrid composites reinforced with flax fabric and polypropylene (PP) hybridized with carbon fibers
findings.consequent: STL per areal density compared to traditional materials like aluminum
findings.quote: Hybrid composites, particularly those reinforced with flax fabric and polypropyl-ene (PP) hybridized with carbon fibers (Fig. 8), have demonstrated STL per areal density significantly higher than traditional materials like aluminum

findings.antecedent: Optimizing carbon fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) composites
findings.consequent: Transmission loss levels comparable to traditional metal materials (especially at lower frequencies)
findings.quote: Optimizing carbon fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) composites can achieve transmission loss levels comparable to traditional metal materials, especially at lower frequencies

findings.antecedent: PP/clay/CNT nanocomposites
findings.consequent: STL (outperforming pure PP at high and low frequencies)
findings.quote: Synergistic effects on STL have been observed in PP/clay/CNT nanocomposites, with the STL for these composites significantly outperforming pure PP at both high and low frequencies

findings.antecedent: Composite rubber reinforced with hollow glass microspheres (HGM)
findings.consequent: Noise reduction capabilities and sound insulation performance
findings.quote: Research on composite rubber reinforced with hollow glass microspheres (HGM) indicates promising noise reduction capa-bilities and excellent sound insulation performance

findings.antecedent: Polymer nanocomposites with nano-clay particles and nanofibers in polyurethane foam
findings.quote: enhancing polymer nanocomposites with nano-clay particles and nanofibers in polyurethane foam can increase STL and the absorption coefficient

findings.antecedent: Wood-waste tire rubber composite panels (WRCP)
findings.consequent: Soundproofing compared to commercial wood particleboard and composite floorboard
findings.quote: They found that these panels exhibit superior soundproofing compared to commercial wood particleboard and composite floorboard.

findings.antecedent: Increasing rubber crumb content and PMDI adhesive level in WRCP
findings.quote: increasing the rubber crumb content and the level of PMDI adhesive in the WRCP enhances its sound insulation properties.

findings.antecedent: Inorganic polymeric foams (IPF) from metakaolin and blast furnace slag with optimal densities
findings.quote: They observed significant STL improvements in IPFs with optimal densities, demonstrating their potential as sound-insulating mate-rials in construction and building applications.

findings.antecedent: Natural and hard-processed woods
findings.consequent: Sound absorption (poor) and sound barrier effectiveness (high STL up to 70 dB)
findings.quote: natural and hard-processed woods were generally poor sound absorbers but effective sound barriers, with maximum transmission loss up to approximately 70 dB.

findings.antecedent: Adding coconut fiber filter mats to hard-processed wood
findings.quote: Adding materials like coconut fiber filter mats significantly improved sound absorption in hard-processed wood.

findings.antecedent: Cork (soft processed wood)
findings.consequent: Sound absorption (mid-frequency) and transmission loss (up to 40 dB)
findings.quote: Cork, classified as a soft processed wood, showed better sound absorption at mid-frequency ranges (500 Hz to 2000 Hz) and had acceptable transmission loss of up to 40 dB.

findings.antecedent: Waste rubber geopolymer concrete (WRGC)
findings.consequent: STL and sound absorption properties compared to conventional concrete
findings.quote: waste rubber geopolymer concrete (WRGC) exhibits superior STL and better sound absorption properties than conventional concrete.

findings.antecedent: Palm panels made from Washingtonia palm tree pruning waste
findings.consequent: Acoustic rating (Class D at low frequencies)
findings.quote: The panels achieved a class D acoustic rating at low frequencies (125 and 250 Hz).

findings.antecedent: Smaller WPCB particle sizes and higher WPCB mass ratios in waste-printed circuit board (WPCB) and unsaturated polyester (UP) composites
findings.consequent: Surface density and stiffness (contributing to better sound insulation)
findings.quote: smaller WPCB particle sizes and higher WPCB mass ratios in the composite enhance surface density and stiffness, contributing to better sound insu-lation.

findings.antecedent: WPCB/UP composites
findings.consequent: Maximum weighted sound reduction index (up to 28.4 dB)
findings.quote: these composite's maximum weighted sound reduction index can reach up to 28.4 dB, suggesting their potential as efficient soundproofing materials.

findings.antecedent: Composites of rice husk waste, expanded cork, and recycled rubber granules
findings.consequent: Weighted reductions in impact SPLs (20 to 27 dB)
findings.quote: The study demonstrates these composites' thermal and acoustic insulation potential, with weighted reductions in impact SPLs ranging from 20 to 27 dB.

findings.antecedent: Recycled ABS reinforced with short cotton fiber waste
findings.consequent: Substantial STL (highest mean value around 70 dB)
findings.quote: The research reveals that these composites exhibit substantial STL, with the highest mean value reaching around 70 dB.

findings.antecedent: Increasing micronized rubber powder (MRP) content in pine particleboard
findings.consequent: STL (slight improvement) and sound absorption (not significantly enhanced)
findings.quote: MRP addition slightly improved STL but did not significantly enhance sound absorption compared to the control sample.

findings.antecedent: Recycled leather cutting waste (LCW)-based acoustic panels
findings.consequent: Sound absorption capabilities (0.2 to 0.7) and STL (up to 30 dB)
findings.quote: The results indicate that the LCW-based panels exhibit significant sound absorption capabilities, with absorption coefficients ranging from 0.2 to 0.7 in the mid-frequency range. The STL values are up to 30 dB

findings.antecedent: Composite insulation panels from recycled cotton fibers and polyethylene/PP packaging wastes
findings.consequent: STL (8 dB) and improved thermal resistance
findings.quote: The panels demonstrated notable STL, reaching 8 dB, and improved thermal resistance

findings.antecedent: Expanded perlite, natural polymers, and rapeseed waste composites
findings.consequent: Sound absorption coefficients at various frequencies
findings.quote: The study showcases significant improvements in sound absorption coefficients at various frequencies

findings.antecedent: Adding high-energy propellant (HEP) waste to fired clay bricks
findings.consequent: STL (depending on orientation and proportion of waste)
findings.quote: adding HEP waste affects the STL depending on the orientation and proportion of waste.

findings.antecedent: Composite panels from natural fibers and rubber crumbs (cotton wool and Kapok)
findings.consequent: Significant STL profiles (Kapok panels up to 47 dB)
findings.quote: panels made from a combination of fiber (cotton wool and Kapok) and rubber crumbs exhibit significant STL profiles, with Kapok panels achieving up to 47 dB.

findings.antecedent: Adding polylactic acid melt-blown nonwoven fabric on rubber crumbs side
findings.quote: Adding polylactic acid melt-blown nonwoven fabric on the rubber crumbs side increases the STL by approximately 20%.

findings.antecedent: Post-consumer recycled denim fabrics with Sorona® or PLA binder fibers
findings.consequent: Sound insulation properties (max transmission loss ~24 dB at 1000 Hz)
findings.quote: incorporating SoronaⓇ or PLA binder fibers with recycled denim fibers enhances the material's sound insulation properties... at around 1000 Hz, these materials achieve a maximum transmission loss of approximately 24 dB

findings.antecedent: Building panels from recycled waste fibers from yarn factories
findings.quote: The STL values range between 24.2 and 32.6 dB, indicating their effectiveness in insulation.

findings.antecedent: Natural rubber-bamboo biochar (NR-BB) composites (10 and 20 phr BB loadings)
findings.quote: STL shows notable enhancements, with an 8% and 11% increase for the 10 and 20 phr BB loadings compared to the NR composites.

findings.antecedent: Increased thickness and blend of blackout and dimout materials in acoustic panels from post-production curtain waste
findings.quote: enhanced sound absorption and transmission loss with increased thickness and the blend of blackout and dimout materials

findings.antecedent: Incorporating 10% by-weight waste jute fabric (WJF) layer into recycled high-density polyethylene (rHDPE) matrix
findings.quote: Incorporating a 10% by-weight WJF layer into the rHDPE matrix significantly enhances tensile strength and modulus... while improving STL performance.

findings.antecedent: Increasing pyrolytic carbon black (PCB) content (to 30 phr) in natural rubber (NR) matrix
findings.quote: the study demonstrates a notable increase in STL of about 17.19% with the NR/PCB30 composite compared to NR/PCB0
